extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology for open scientific research in computational linguistics. It includes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We start by crawling the PDF files and metadata from the source ACL Anthology. We then pass the PDF files through the full-text extraction process. We enhance this data using Semantic Scholar’s API to fetch additional information about OCL papers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology, plus additional information fetched from Semantic Scholar’s API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 1952 to September 2022, with annual updates for newly added papers.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is biased toward peer-reviewed and open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology, and it underrepresents other sources and topics; the authors also note declining underrepresented topics such as "Discourse and Pragmatics" and "Phonology, Morphology and Word Segmentation."
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus is small-scale and not comprehensive; it excludes sources beyond ACL Anthology, may need expansion with arXiv papers, may contain lower-quality arXiv papers if expanded, uses only open-source PDF-to-text tools due to budget constraints, and is unlabeled, so it lacks annotations for tasks requiring labels.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus is intended to advance open research in computational linguistics and support temporal topic trend analysis; it also highlights emerging ethics-related topics, suggesting relevance to responsible NLP research.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for open research in computational linguistics, including existing research tasks and temporal topic trends analysis; the authors also suggest it could support training silver labels and human-AI collaborative annotations for downstream tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to update OCL yearly to keep it current with ACL Anthology data and aim to host the data on ACL Anthology itself via full-text extraction and information extraction APIs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Model-predicted silver topic labels were generated and released; the paper says they "extrapolate and integrate the model predictions as silver-labeled topic information in the OCL."
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files and metadata were crawled from ACL Anthology; PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed; full texts were extracted from PDFs using GROBID; figures and tables were extracted from PDFs using PDFFigures; language was detected using a public language detection toolkit with title and abstract as inputs.
